column1: # The ring's call sites of sub_82C04DF0 as the LISTINGS give them (Session 101, lane 194; the oracle of tools\ring\ring_rows_test.cpp reads this table, NOT the stream's values).

# Sources: docs\systems\ring.md Part A section 1 (G+ offsets, stores 0x824EB6DC-0x824EBD58 of sub_824EB648), Part D (call sites, r5 meaning), SKIP_GAME_WORK_MAP.md 16.1 / 16.2 (calls a frame, the three
# heights sharing one r5). Marks: C = read in a listing / image word, T = a TEST PARAMETER (a number the listings do not give; the test chooses it so every rule of the reader is exercised).

# Columns (tab separated): class, g_offset (byte offset of the model pointer in the object at [0x836F4C74]), caller, call_site (the guest address ring.md Part D cites: the `lwz rX,<slot offset>(rY)` that loads the vtable slot, or the bctrl for the ropes; the selftest finds the load within 12 bytes before it), vtable_slot_offset, r5_rule,
#   calls_per_frame, sides, heights, nodes, count_path, marks

# r5_rule: model200 = r5 is [model+200] of the model (every instance of a model shares it; the game writes the instance's rows into it before each submit); rope_buf = r5 is X + 29184 + 8192 * side (a buffer
#   owned by the rope context, shared by a side's heights, rewritten between heights).
# count_path: direct = [model+296] != 0 and [model+300] = the node count; forward = [model+296] == 0, [model+220] = a sub-object whose own slot 2 gives the count (verified, then followed).
# sides/heights: rope classes only (calls_per_frame = sides * heights); other classes 0 0.
